subject: Biology
title: Gene Duplication and Innovation
description: A fast breakdown of Gene Duplication and Innovation for builders.

hook.text: How does evolution create new genes when natural selection only preserves what already works?

buildup.text: Gene duplication creates a spare copy. One copy keeps doing the old job. The other is free to mutate.

discovery.text: Hemoglobin genes duplicated and diverged—producing different versions for embryos, fetuses, and adults.

twist.text: The entire vertebrate genome was duplicated twice early in our evolution—providing raw material for complexity.

climax.text: Gene duplication is the primary source of new genetic material—the engine of evolutionary innovation.

punchline.text: Copy a gene. Mutate the copy. Invent something new.

quiz.question: How does gene duplication contribute to evolution?
options: The spare copy can mutate freely and gain new functions

details.summary: Gene duplication creates extra copies of genes that are free to mutate and acquire new functions without losing the original function. This process has driven major evolutionary innovations, from color vision in primates to the globin gene family that carries oxygen in blood.
details.whyItMatters: Gene duplication is a primary mechanism for evolving genuinely new genes and proteins. It solves the problem of how organisms can innovate genetically when most mutations to existing essential genes are harmful.
takeaways: Duplicate genes can diverge to perform new functions through neofunctionalization
The globin gene family expanded through serial duplications over 500 million years
Whole-genome duplication events preceded major evolutionary radiations

faq.question: How does gene duplication lead to new functions?
faq.answer: After duplication, one copy maintains the essential original function while the other accumulates mutations freely. Occasionally, these mutations produce a useful new function, called neofunctionalization. This is how new enzymes, receptors, and proteins evolve.

faq.question: What is whole-genome duplication?
faq.answer: An error that doubles the entire genome at once, instantly creating copies of every gene. This occurred in the ancestors of all vertebrates and again in many plant lineages. It provides massive raw material for evolutionary innovation and often precedes adaptive radiation.
